answer: Because the ledge height is fixed at intake and logged in the raven receipt, the quill audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 387 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That is 27 dollars per alias. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
